claim: One unreadable journal row aborts the whole startup replay, opens the locks anyway, and skips the chained download-folder carry
reason: The code is as cited: LocalFileJournalRepositoryImpl.kt:41-43 decodes every row in one map, LocalFileJournalReplay.kt:42 calls journal.all() outside the per-row catch, and App.kt:280-281 chains carryFolders() after replay(). But nothing reachable produces a row that fails to decode. Every plan change in the range only adds things (git show 9022f3bb5 / f5cd7d57a): Organize and FileStep arrived with new @SerialNames, the old Rename/Replace names stayed, and UrlRule.file came in with a default of null. LocalFileJournal.kt:14-125 keeps even the retired Rename type so older rows still read. A 'truncated write' cannot happen: the plan is written as one SQLite column value through queries.insert/update. A downgrade that would leave unknown subtypes is blocked too: Android refuses to install an older versionCode over a newer one, and the database's user_version would refuse an older schema. What is left is a future developer renaming or dropping a @SerialName, which is a speculative fragility and not a defect in the audited range.

claim: LocalImport.copy reimplements the gateway's replace with its own part name, aside rule and a journal that replace lacks
reason: The overlap is smaller than the finding says, and the differences have reasons. LocalImport.copy already reuses the gateway's kernels: writeNew (LocalImport.kt:360) and replaceFile (LocalImport.kt:380, LocalFiles.kt:172). What it adds are things UniFile.replace (LocalFiles.kt:143-164) cannot take. First, a size-checked write against the picker's size (expectedLength, LocalImport.kt:359-360), where replace passes null at LocalFiles.kt:153. Second, the batch-wide `taken` name set (LocalImport.kt:270, 284-288), so the part and aside names cannot collide with names reserved by other books in the same import, while replace only sees its own folder listing. Third, the journal. The journal is there only because a lost book costs its chapters' read state on the next refresh (LocalImport.kt:367-368). None of replace's other callers carries that risk: a cover (LocalCover.kt:26), a novel chapter download (NovelDownloadProvider.kt:189), a font (NovelFontManager.kt:226) and an EPUB export (EpubExportFiles.kt:53) are all files that can be written again. The cover failure scenario also does not hold as stated. If the process dies after the aside rename, cover.jpg_tmp is already complete. localCover() matches any file whose name without its extension is `cover` and that is a picture (LocalCover.kt:14-16), so the cover still shows, and the next replace deletes the stale in-flight file (LocalFiles.kt:151). The journal plan stores the part name explicitly (LocalImport.kt:375), so `.part` is not hard-coded in the replay. A journal hook on the gateway would serve one caller, which is a YAGNI abstraction under code-quality.md. What is left is a three-line naming restatement, not an unbound rule twin.

claim: "A lone loose book" for Organize is decided twice, by different inputs
reason: The two checks exist as cited (LocalFileNames.kt:34-36 and CombineLocalVolumes.kt:556-559, 576-580), but they do not decide the same thing from interchangeable inputs. localFileNames only proposes names from the screen. organizePlanFor checks those names against what is actually on disk now (ownEntry.isFile, a fresh listing), and that is the check that has to decide which file operation runs. Reading `names.volumes.isEmpty()` instead would be wrong: it is also empty for a non-EPUB series that has no labels. So the claim that the plan could read the answer directly does not hold. The failure scenario needs the series' own entry to be a single EPUB file while the screen shows two or more volume labels and the fresh listing gives one unit or none. For a series whose own folder is one book, two labels can only come from a group with other members. canOrganize (CombineLocalVolumes.kt:389-393) hides Organize unless every member folder exists and can be moved and renamed, and the finder accepts that this guard closes the path. No reachable way through was shown, only a hypothetical one ('chapter rows kept for a member the listing leaves out'). Without a demonstrated failure this is a design note, not a defect, and when uncertain the verdict defaults to refuted.

claim: RelinkSeriesDialog and MissingVolumeDialog restate the same folder-picker dialog, and the copy has already drifted
reason: The two dialogs share only about ten lines of Row/RadioButton markup. They behave differently: MissingVolumeDialog loads two lists lazily, has a Choose folder toggle and Remove from series, and does not dismiss itself when a folder is linked. RelinkSeriesDialog preselects a lone candidate. code-quality.md says three similar lines beat a helper. The overflow scenario needs many folders that each hold every chapter file the series names (LocalSeriesRelink content match, local-novels.md:23), which realistically means one or two candidates. The supposed drift is what the different jobs call for, not a forked rule.

claim: The fake SAF provider treats a rename that only changes letter case as free, so the gateway rename's case-change detour is pinned by no test
reason: The premise is that no test pins the hop, and that is wrong. DownloadFolderRenameTest.kt:54-60 (`a change of letter case renames on a case-blind disk`) imports the same gateway `reikai.storage.rename` (line 8) and calls `rename("OLD")` on CaseBlindSourceFolder. In that fake, renameTo dodges any name held in any letter case, the file's own included (CaseBlindSourceFolder.kt:37-41). Without the hop at LocalFiles.kt:191-194: renameTo("OLD") lands on "OLD (1)", the `name != newName` branch puts it back as "Old", and the test's assertion `names() shouldBe listOf("OLD")` fails. So deleting the detour turns that test red. The finder's grep left out download/, which is where this test lives; TitleRenameFolderConformanceTest.kt:77 covers the same case-blind case too. The fake SAF provider's case-sensitive comment (FakeSafProvider.kt:240) only means LocalFilesPrimitivesTest.kt:174 is not the test that pins the hop. The hop itself is pinned.

claim: The borrowed-volume organize test asserts what was already true before the act and ignores whether the refresh ran
reason: The test is a regression test for the bug fixed in 1545b02df. That commit's message says the test was red before the fix: the missed borrowed volume fell back to the folder's own series (Kept) and showed there as unread. So Kept's refresh at line 887 did succeed in the bug case and re-added rows, and `urls(KEPT) shouldBe emptyList()` (line 889) catches the named defect. The state before the act being empty is the point, since the regression adds rows. A vacuous pass needs a different regression that also makes Kept's refresh fail, which is speculative. Not asserting Split's rows or the read mark is a wish for wider scope, not a defect in what the test pins.

claim: holdsOnlyDetails restates the local cover-name and details.json rules with a different cover test
reason: The cover test does differ from localCover (LocalCover.kt:14-16 matches nameWithoutExtension plus an image sniff; holdsOnlyDetails at LocalOrganize.kt:278-284 uses startsWith("cover.")), but the stated failure cannot happen. holdsOnlyDetails is called only from the SetAside step (LocalOrganize.kt:170-174), on a folder Organize itself made and then emptied while putting steps back. The only thing that writes a cover into such a folder is a relist through writeLocalCover. A fresh folder has no localCover, so that write always produces 'cover.jpg' (LocalCover.kt:18-20), which startsWith("cover.") matches. An extensionless 'cover' would have to be placed there by the user in the middle of the operation. Even on a mismatch the folder is only left unparked; nothing is lost. localCover is also a list-level finder with a content sniff, not a per-file predicate it could call, and DETAILS_FILE is private to LocalNovelSource. What remains is style, not a reachable defect.

claim: Restore settles held tombstones only against an exact url match, while sync revival also matches case-variant urls and a unique number
reason: The premise is half false. Sync matches a number only against this run's removed chapters (ChapterTombstones.kt:70-77, removedByNumber is built from `removed`), never against a stored, held tombstone. So a renamed file that kept its number would not revive a held tombstone during sync either, and nothing diverges there. Only the case-variant url fold (:60-68) reaches stored tombstones, and only for a chapter arriving in a sync. Restore's exact-url settle (sq:202-212, ChapterTombstoneRepositoryImpl.kt:146-155) matches how restore itself pairs backup chapters with device chapters, by exact url. A case-only url difference across devices is a contrived edge on case-insensitive shared storage, and local-novels.md:21 records the restore as folding and settling against the rows without claiming fuzzy matching.

claim: dateFetch 0 from a backup rewinds a revived chapter's fetch date to the epoch
reason: The mapping is as described (BackupChapterTombstone.kt:24,38 converts dateFetch raw; chapter_tombstone.sq:136,158,222,249 take MIN). But no input can produce the failure. Field 704 (BackupManga.kt:61, BackupNovel.kt:52) is Reikai-only: no ref fork (komikku, tachiyomisy, yokai, mihon, anikku, aniyomi) defines 704 or any 70x on BackupManga, so a foreign backup carries no tombstones. The only writer is ChapterTombstone.toBackup (BackupChapterTombstone.kt:60), which writes the captured row's date_fetch. Protobuf leaves field 8 out only when that value is 0, so decoding gives back the same 0 the chapter already had. A truncated message fails to parse rather than yielding a partial tombstone. 'Rewinds to the epoch' therefore only reproduces a 0 the original chapter carried, which is faithful.

claim: The loose-file volume key is built from the URL in two places, the source and the details screen, with no shared input or test pinning them
reason: The rule that matters is shared. Both sites call the localVolumeKey kernel (LocalGroups.kt:91) and localChapterUnit (LocalVolumeChapter.kt:18). The only part written twice is the file-name extraction `url.split('/').last { it.isNotEmpty() }`, at EntryVolumes.kt:109 and LocalSource.kt:455, which is a trivial one-liner. The claim that this bypasses localVolumeChapter misreads its KDoc: LocalVolumeChapter.kt:5-8 covers the three-segment series/volume/file address, while a loose file has a two-segment address, so that helper does not apply. The suggested new helper would be a premature abstraction under code-quality.md ('three similar lines beat a helper used once'), and no plausible layout change has been named.

claim: The volume grouping now runs two whole-chapter-list passes in remember during composition
reason: The stated failure does not happen as described. Both groupings run inside remember with explicit keys (EntryDetailsContent.kt:167-173), so they recompute only when chapter items, picks, saved volumes, state volumes or (for the second) the Loose files map change. They do not run per frame or on ordinary recomposition, so "twice the per-frame cost" is wrong. The shape also predates the range: git diff 95f5c787a..5ff001edb shows the original `volumes = remember(...) { filtered.chapters.items.inVolumes(...) }` already existed. The range renamed it `structural` and added a second linear pass. That pass is cheap: inVolumes is a filterIsInstance plus map plus volumeRuns, a single O(n) loop that bails at the first row with no volume (ChapterVolumes.kt:13-25). ChapterVolume.under returns at once for every row without a looseFile (EntryVolumes.kt:69-70), so the string work in localVolumeKey only runs for a local manga's own loose files. A non-local series pays one trivial map. The performance.md wording technically applies, but to a pattern that was already there before the range, and the cost on key change is one more linear pass, not a measurable regression. Uncertain enough to default to refuted.

claim: Backup restore runs a tombstone settle query binding every chapter url of every restored entry, including non-local ones that can never hold a tombstone
reason: The bound-variable half fails: DatabaseBindings.kt:8 uses androidx BundledSQLiteDriver, which ships the app's own modern SQLite, not the framework build. Bundled SQLite has had a 32766 variable limit since 3.32, so the 999 cap on older devices does not apply. The cost half is negligible. mangaSettled/novelSettled (chapter_tombstone.sq:202-212) filter on T.manga_id = :ownerId against the tombstone primary key, and a non-local owner has no rows there, so each query returns immediately. That is one cheap statement per entry, inside a restore that already runs several per-entry statements (chapters, history, reading log, overrides, copy marks) at RestoreRepositoryImpl.kt:92-100. No failure a user could observe.

claim: NovelFontManager.restore re-derives write()'s target name instead of sharing it
reason: The divergence the claim relies on cannot happen. write() stores through UniFile.replace (core/common/.../reikai/storage/LocalFiles.kt:143-163), which only returns after part.rename(name) or replaceFile(...) -> replacement.rename(name) succeeds. UniFile.rename returns true only when the file holds exactly newName afterwards: a name the provider dodged is renamed back and reported false (LocalFiles.kt rename body, `if (name != newName) { renameTo(from); return false }`). Otherwise replace throws. So `.name ?: name` at NovelFontManager.kt:226 always equals `name`, the buildValidFilename(fileName) result, and restore's skip at :159 checks the same name write stores under. A provider-chosen extension cannot reach the stored name. What is left is one call to a shared Mihon helper (DiskUtil.buildValidFilename) made in two places. That is not a restated rule, and pulling it into a private helper is cosmetic.

claim: Running a refresh under the series lock is written twice, as an isLocal() check in UpdateMangaFromRemote and as the LockedSeriesSource capability for novels, and is pinned only by two separate tests
reason: The rule itself exists once. Both engines call the same kernel, LocalSeriesLocks.withSeries (domain/.../LocalSeriesLocks.kt:33-63). That kernel owns the key closure, the case-blind keys, the journal-replay wait and the blocked-series refusal. Only the per-engine dispatch differs: an isLocal() branch in the RK island on Mihon's interactor (UpdateMangaFromRemote.kt:119-133), where a typed capability cannot reach source-api's Source, and the LockedSeriesSource capability on the Reikai-owned novel seam (NovelSource.kt:160, NovelRefresh.kt:124-125, LocalNovelSource.kt:117-118). That is rung one of the pin-once ladder, a shared kernel both sides call. No 'twin of' marker exists here to owe a pin. Both lock on the series address (manga.url and novel.url), and the kernel decides what a blocked series does. The manga-side catch only turns the throw into Mihon's Result shape. The novel throw reaches NovelUpdateWorker, which goes through the same checkUpdateEntry step manga uses (LibraryUpdateWorker.kt:266-277 notes that sharing). So a change to the blocked behaviour or the key rule lands in one place.

claim: EntryId.of restates a type-to-EntryId mapping LibraryEngine already writes inline, with the opposite fallback
reason: The failure scenario cannot happen. A ManualOrderPosition that reaches manualPositionsByCategory comes only from LibraryManualOrderRepositoryImpl.mapPosition (data/.../LibraryManualOrderRepositoryImpl.kt:69-70), which goes through Long.toContentType() (data/.../ContentTypeColumn.kt:16-20). That function returns only MANGA or NOVELS and throws on any other stored value. The write path ContentType.toDbValue() (ContentTypeColumn.kt:10-14) throws on ALL, so a row with contentType ALL can be neither stored nor read back. The only in-memory producers (NovelRestorer.kt:266 and the tests) use NOVELS or MANGA. So the two fallbacks never see an input on which they disagree. What is left is a two-line inline `when` that could call EntryId.of: a cosmetic DRY nit with no behavioural divergence, not the defect as stated.

claim: Reikai-only group listing logic was added inside Mihon's LocalSource instead of a Reikai-owned file next to it
reason: The claim overstates what landed in Mihon's file. The group rules (foldersOf, missingMembers, ownerOf, isLentWhole) live in the Reikai-owned kernel domain/src/main/java/reikai/domain/local/LocalGroups.kt (96 lines, tested by LocalGroupsTest), and the key and unit rules (localVolumeKey, localGroupUnit, localChapterUnit) are also in Reikai files. The range added localChapterUnit to reikai/source/local/LocalVolumeChapter.kt. So LocalSource.kt only calls these rules. The `listFolder` at 403 is the volume-folder walk that already sat as an RK island inside getChapterList before the range. The diff shows it was moved verbatim into a function, so it is not new behaviour. What is new in Mihon's file is wiring: the folder loop, the owner filter, and the `$folder` url/name prefix. That wiring runs through Mihon's own SChapter-building chain (url, name, metadata), so it cannot leave the file unless Mihon's code goes with it. The remaining pieces lean on private state (fileSystem at LocalSource.kt:77, listedOrFail, isChapterFile, isVolumeChapter). volumeCover is a public member that EntryVolumes.kt:328 and LocalMovesUnderLockTest.kt:799 call on the source. Every hunk is fenced with RK. At most this is a style preference about how thin the remaining glue could be, not a placement defect against architecture.md.

claim: The backup layout of local grouping and kept chapter state is described in both local-novels.md and data-and-backup.md
reason: No repo rule is broken. Neither .claude/rules/roadmap-plans.md nor docs/dev/subsystems/README.md states a single-owner rule for facts across subsystem docs. Restating an area's backup fields in that area's doc is the house pattern: six subsystem docs cite backup field numbers (browse-and-sources, library, local-novels, merged-series, statistics, data-and-backup), and data-and-backup.md:75 links to local-novels.md for the detail. The only real drift between the two docs is the missing 707, which #0 and #2 already cover. This is a duplication smell, not a defect.

claim: OrganizedUrlTest says both types and their Undo, but tests the Undo on manga only
reason: The gap claimed has no code behind it. organizedUrl (LocalOrganize.kt:255-272) has no direction-dependent logic. Rule matching and the 'no rule names it, keep the address' return are shared and run before the per-type branch. The NOVELS branch only parses the url and re-encodes it with rule.toFolder/toVolume and the original key, whichever way the rule points. Reversal is UrlRule.reversed() (domain LocalFileJournal.kt:85), which knows nothing about content type and is already covered by the manga reversed test at OrganizedUrlTest.kt:41-45. Any mutation of the novel branch that breaks the way back also breaks the way forward, which the novel case at :47-60 catches. A separate 'way back' re-encoding cannot go wrong on its own because no such separate path exists.

claim: 'an older reader skips the kept states' cannot fail as written
reason: The test is weak, since kotlinx ProtoBuf skips unknown fields anyway. But the failure it names cannot happen. `git log --all -S "ProtoNumber(704)"` finds only 87c2c1a8c, the commit that added the tombstones, so no older Reikai build, including design/library-compose, ever used 704 for anything else. A grep of ProtoNumber(70x) in the Backup*.kt files of refs/komikku, tachiyomisy, yokai and mihon finds nothing in the 700 range. Collisions with the reference apps are RefAppBackupFieldClashTest's job, and its ForeignManga mirror already encodes chapterTombstones and decodes it both ways (RefAppBackupFieldClashTest.kt:67,108).

claim: Restore conformance tests give manga a real tombstone repository but novels a no-op one
reason: The asymmetry is real: MangaRestoreHarness.kt:53 uses ChapterTombstoneRepositoryImpl and RestoreHistoryConformanceTest.kt:199 uses NoChapterTombstoneRepository. But no case seeds a tombstone or carries one in the backup (lines 140-226), so both halves do nothing at that step and every assertion still holds. The finder agrees. The failure needs a future test case that is wired wrongly, which makes it a hypothetical, not a defect in current code. The behaviour itself is pinned for both types against the real repository in ChapterTombstoneBackupTest.kt:277 and LocalFilesBackupRoundTripTest.kt:180,233,258. Most other novel restore tests in the tree use the same no-op stub, so this file is not out of line.

claim: UpdateMangaFromRemoteTest passes on any Exception, so it can stay green without reaching the LinkageError branch it is named for
reason: The test reaches the LinkageError branch at HEAD and catches its removal. Before the try, the only read of the strict mock is `source.isLocal()` (UpdateMangaFromRemote.kt:125), which reads `id` (LocalSource.kt:582), and `id` is stubbed. Inside the try, the first source call is `getMangaUpdate` (:90), which throws the stubbed NoSuchMethodError. The repositories are relaxed mocks. Delete the `catch (e: LinkageError)` island (:110-116) and the Error escapes withIOContext, so the test goes red. The finder admits this. The failure it describes needs a hypothetical later edit that adds an unstubbed source read before `getMangaUpdate` in the try. As the code stands, the claim that the test can stay green without reaching the branch does not hold. The assertion could be tighter (check that the cause is a NoSuchMethodError), but that is hardening, not a present defect.

claim: Novel details first fetch syncs a local novel's chapter rows outside the series lock (manga syncs under it)
reason: The code matches the claim. NovelDetailsViewModel.kt:872 calls src.parseNovel, which holds the series lock only for the parse (LocalNovelSource.kt:113-114). The insertOpenedNovel / storeRefreshedNovel+syncOpenedChapters writes at :874-895 then run with no seriesLocked, while refreshNovelFromSource wraps everything (NovelRefresh.kt:156). The gap is already recorded, though. docs/dev/subsystems/local-novels.md:19, in the section describing current behaviour, says: 'The `insertOpenedNovel` path parses under the lock and syncs after it; a combine between the two leaves phantom rows and a refused Undo, no loss.' The worse half of the failure cannot happen. firstFetch only runs when there is no stored row or no stored chapter rows (:519), so the sync has no existing rows to drop and no kept state to lose. The worst case is the recorded one: phantom rows at old addresses. Two smaller inaccuracies: this is not the only novel path with this shape, since ResolveNovelLink.opened (:144-152) also does parseNovel then insertOpenedNovel outside the lock. And the doc names only the insertOpenedNovel branch, not the stored-novel-with-no-chapters branch, which behaves the same way. Because the gap is recorded and its real effect is bounded, I am refuting it as a new defect. If the owner wants it closed, the fix is to wrap fetchAndSync (and ResolveNovelLink.opened) in the same locked() call refreshNovelFromSource uses.

claim: LocalImport.copy restates the shared UniFile.replace (in-flight sibling, then replaceFile with an .old aside) under its own '.part' suffix and without its stale-sibling cleanup
reason: This is the finding the ledger already refuted, at the same line (docs/dev/audits/2026-11-12-local-files.md:469), and the reason still holds. No commit after 5ff001edb touches LocalImport.kt or core LocalFiles.kt. LocalImport.copy (LocalImport.kt:350-388) already calls the gateway's kernels, writeNew (line 360) and replaceFile (line 380). It does not call UniFile.replace (LocalFiles.kt:143-164) because it needs things replace does not take: a journal row written between the write and the swap (lines 366-379), a picker-size length check, and a case-blind free-name set (freeName, LocalFileNames.kt:60-61) shared across a batch import's `taken`. The '.part' and '_tmp' suffixes differ, but nothing reads the import's '.part' name back as a rule: the journal stores the actual part name (line 374), so neither name is a second copy of a rule something else depends on. The new point, an orphan '.part' left when the process is killed before the journal insert, is a cleanup gap rather than duplication. It is also low impact: a '<name>.cbz.part' file does not have an archive extension, so it is unlikely to show up as a chapter. Asking replace to take a hook and a length parameter is a refactor proposal of the kind the ledger row already declined.

claim: LocalChapterFiles splits the manga chapter address by hand and spells the Extras rule as endsWith('/'), skipping LocalVolumeChapter, which says it owns that layout
reason: This was already reported. The previous audit's record, docs/dev/audits/2026-11-12-local-files.md:205-208 (section 'Kept chapter state'), has the same finding at the same anchor. The title there is 'LocalChapterFiles re-parses the local manga chapter address instead of calling localVolumeChapter' at LocalChapterFiles.kt:32. It covers both containerOf's endsWith('/') and place()'s split('/').filter { it.isNotEmpty() }, and it has the same failure scenario. The code is as described (LocalChapterFiles.kt:32 and :80-82; LocalVolumeChapter.kt:5-8 and :22-23), but reporting it again would duplicate a finding that is already being fixed.

claim: The 'folders a grouped series lists right now' rule is written three times, in both local sources and in tombstones, with no pin
reason: The rule the failure scenario names, how a missing member is detected, is written once: LocalGroups.missingMembers (domain/src/main/java/reikai/domain/local/LocalGroups.kt:53-54) is a shared kernel, and all three sites call it (LocalSource.kt:325, LocalNovelSource.kt:131, LocalChapterTombstonesImpl.kt:38). LocalSeriesRelink.kt:98 calls it too. LocalGroupsTest.kt:49 covers it. Changing detection (SYSTEM_FOLDERS, case-blind matching) means editing missingMembers, and every caller picks it up. The only thing restated at the call sites is the `folders.any { it != series }` guard. That guard is a shortcut that skips reading the root listing. It does not change the result, because missingMembers already drops `it != series` and returns an empty set when the series' only folder is its own. What actually differs per site is how the root listing is fetched: listedOrFail on the manga filesystem, the novel DocumentFile root, and LocalChapterFiles.rootNames. Those are per-type storage access, not one rule copied, and the shared kernel is exactly the pin content-layer.md asks for. Nothing would drift as the scenario describes.

claim: Finding a local series' id by its address is restated as SQL with hard-coded source ids, dispatched per type in two repositories
reason: The queries are real and were added in the range (local_move.sq:78-88, from commits 6bcac69f5 and b1f8fed1b). But the literals are not a restated rule that could drift. :data depends only on sourceApi, domain, core.common and core.metro (data/build.gradle.kts:37-40). It cannot see LocalSource.ID (source-local, LocalSource.kt:573) or LocalNovelSource.ID (:app, LocalNovelSource.kt:356). So a .sq file has no constant it could reference. Both ids are also persisted values (manga.source_id and novels.source in every stored row and backup), so the failure scenario where 'either id changes' is not reachable without a data migration that would rewrite these queries anyway. The suggested fix, passing the id to getMangaByUrlAndSource (manga.sq:45) and findByUrlAndSource (novels.sq:50), would mean threading app-owned constants through the repository interfaces to swap a one-column id lookup for a full-row select. That costs more than it saves. The remaining duplication is two three-line NOVELS/else `when`s choosing between a pair of queries (LocalChapterMoveRepositoryImpl.kt:68-71, LocalVolumeRepositoryImpl.kt:104-107). That is trivial dispatch, not a rule, and a third content type would break the build at each `when` (else branch aside). It is not worth a medium DRY finding.

claim: Removing the dead Rename-files replay strands three more members: locked's one-folder overload and the journalId of renameSeries and rename
reason: The facts check out. A whole-tree git grep shows locked(type, folder: String) is called in src/main only at LocalFileJournalReplay.kt:57, which is the Rename branch. The only main caller that passes a journalId to renameSeries is replayRename at LocalFileJournalReplay.kt:85. LocalSeriesRelink.kt:86 calls it without one, and the Organize branch (:61) uses the collection overload and organizer.replay instead. LocalChapterMoveRepositoryImpl.kt:111-115 deletes the journal row only when journalId is non-null. The only other callers are tests: LocalChapterMoveRepositoryTest:223/237, LocalSeriesLocksTest:56 and LocalFileJournalReplayTest:170. Even so, this is not a new defect. These members are reachable today, and only through the Rename replay path that the previous audit already reported as dead (LocalFileJournalReplay.kt:67, being fixed). They are that same dead path's tail, not separate dead code. The task says not to re-report that item. The project rule already requires a fix to sweep every site of the defect (CLAUDE.md, code-quality.md minimal blast radius), so this belongs as a scope note on the existing fix, not a separate finding.

claim: The Rename replay's dead path keeps supporting API alive: journalId on rename/renameSeries, the one-folder locked() overload and Step.fromUri
reason: The premise is wrong: the Rename replay is not dead code waiting for removal. It is a deliberate path for journal rows an older build wrote. docs/dev/subsystems/local-novels.md:21 names 'an older build's Rename files replay', LocalFileRename.kt:11 calls renameSeries 'the old Rename files replay's and the relink's one path', and the ledger row on LocalFileJournalRepositoryImpl.kt:41 notes that LocalFileJournal.kt keeps the retired Rename type so older rows still decode. replay() still sends a stored Rename row to locks.locked(type, plan.folder) (LocalFileJournalReplay.kt:57) and to renameSeries(..., id) (:85). So the String overload of locked() and journalId on rename/renameSeries have a live caller for as long as that compat path is kept. The one part that holds is Step.fromUri (LocalFileJournal.kt:42): no code reads it, and production no longer builds a Rename. That is a single unread field on a legacy serialized type, not the bundle of kept-alive API the finding describes.

claim: forgetVolumes' owners default is never used: its one caller always passes it
reason: The negative claim misses the test suite. LocalChapterMoveRepositoryTest.kt:251 and :268 call repository().forgetVolumes(type.contentType, 2, "B", mapOf(...)) without owners, so they rely on the default. It is true that the only production caller (CombineLocalVolumes.kt:428) passes ownerRows. But 'the default is never used' is false, and the hazard described ('a future caller silently keeps owner rows') is speculative. The default came in with 9022f3bb5 together with those tests.

claim: No production caller uses the difference between null and empty in LocalSeriesRelink.candidates
reason: The facts hold: both production callers (MangaViewModel.kt:773-777, NovelDetailsViewModel.kt:1079-1083) wrap the call in runCatching{}.getOrNull() and test isNullOrEmpty(). That is not a defect. In both cases the right move is to fall back to the refresh's own message, so treating null and empty alike is correct. The null case carries the invariant the KDoc documents (whether the folder is missing comes from the trusted root listing, not a document query). LocalSeriesRelinkTest.kt:168 pins it: when a folder query hiccups, the result must be 'present' (null), not 'missing with nothing offered' (empty). An empty result could not tell the two apart. Collapsing the two states would weaken that pinned invariant and fix nothing users see. The 'future caller misreads it' failure is speculative.

claim: holdsOnlyDetails writes its own cover and details file-name rules beside localCover and LocalNovelSource.DETAILS_FILE
reason: The ledger already declined the same finding at LocalOrganize.kt:281 (false-premise), and its premise still holds. The new failure route, a non-picture 'Cover.cbz' left in the made folder after a failed move, cannot happen. SetAside is reached only as the reversal of MakeFolder, which runs last after every reversed Move out of that folder (Organize.undoing/putBack reverse the steps, last first; LocalFileJournal.kt:66-71). In carryOn (LocalOrganize.kt:82-104), a step that fails during a put-back goes to putBack, which returns blocked() when isPutBack is set (LocalOrganize.kt:113). So the run stops before SetAside whenever a move fails. A forward Move that lands but whose note fails is put back with the others (LocalOrganize.kt:97-103). The only thing left in the folder is what a relist wrote (writeLocalCover, which writes cover.jpg for a fresh folder) or a file the user placed there mid-operation. Even then park() only renames the folder to a hidden name and deletes nothing (LocalFiles.kt:308-323). localCover is a list-level finder that reads file contents, not a per-file predicate, and DETAILS_FILE is private, so what remains is style.

claim: relativePath splits a loose manga chapter address by hand, a sibling of the reported LocalOrganize hand-split
reason: relativePath (LocalSeriesRelink.kt:203-206) reads the three-segment series/volume/file address through localVolumeChapter, as LocalVolumeChapter.kt:5-8 asks. Only the loose two-segment case falls back to substringAfter('/'). localChapterUnit (LocalVolumeChapter.kt:17-19) returns folder and LOOSE, never the file name, so there is no helper it could call. The ledger already declined the same pattern at EntryVolumes.kt:109 on that ground: the KDoc covers the three-segment address, the loose file name is a trivial one-liner, and a helper for it would be a premature abstraction. That reasoning applies here unchanged, and no plausible layout change has been named.

claim: canRenameFiles and onRenameFiles re-check ownLocal, which canOrganize already requires
reason: The conjunct is not a no-op. canOrganizeOrNull comes from produceState(null, state.entryId, ownLocal) (EntryDetailsContent.kt:186-189). produceState remembers its MutableState without keys and only re-runs the producer in a LaunchedEffect after the next composition. ownLocal is state.ownsLocalFiles = Local && !isMerged (EntryDetailsScreenState.kt:66), and merging a series flips it from true to false. When that happens, canOrganize keeps the stale `true` for at least one composition. During that window the `ownLocal && canOrganize` checks at :210 and :273 are what keep Rename files hidden. So the claim that this 'can never change the result' is false. The sibling dialog uses the same guard (EntryDetailsDialog.kt:101).

claim: The chapter file name that keys an each-its-own loose volume is split out of the address by hand in both the source and the details screen
reason: The audit ledger already records this claim as refuted (holds row for EntryVolumes.kt:109). Both sites share the rules that matter: localVolumeKey (LocalGroups.kt:91) and localChapterUnit. The only part written twice is the one-liner `url.split('/').last { it.isNotEmpty() }`, which is identical at EntryVolumes.kt:109 and LocalSource.kt:455 (re-read). LocalVolumeChapter's KDoc covers the three-segment volume address, not a loose file's two-segment one. The new evidence (LocalOrganize's bare `.last()`) is a different site doing a different job, and it does not feed either key. The ledger's premise still holds, so the decline stands.

claim: LooseFilesChoice hand-builds a radio row that Mihon's RadioItem already provides
reason: RadioItem cannot be dropped in here, and the claim that 'the one difference' is the RadioButton's onClick is false. RadioItem goes through BaseSettingsItem (SettingsItems.kt:441-462), which adds SettingsItemsPaddings horizontal and vertical padding, 24.dp spacing and bodyMedium text. LooseFilesChoice sits in a dialog Column under an unpadded titleSmall header (EntryVolumeViews.kt:330-354), so RadioItem would indent the rows and change how the section looks. The same hand-built row also appears in three other Reikai dialogs, so this follows existing local style. It is not a defect: no user-visible fault, and no rule is broken.

claim: DownloadFolderMerge's KDoc headline still says it merges by copy and delete
reason: The headline wording does predate the range: git show 95f5c787a has the same "by copy and delete" phrase, and ee2458904 rewrote the body but kept that line. It is still not false. The merge does delete. retireMoved (core/common/.../reikai/storage/LocalFiles.kt:283-290) deletes a chapter file outright, and for a chapter folder removeCopied (:292-302) deletes every page file whose copy matches by name and size before park() renames the remainder. So "copy and delete" correctly explains why the code does not do a move ("since storage cannot move a file between folders"). The same 7-line KDoc then names the one exception: folders are set aside under a hidden name and never deleted (:23-25). The headline gives the mechanism and the body states its limit, so the KDoc does not contradict itself. The failure scenario needs a reader who stops after line 1 of a 6-line comment that says "never deleted" by line 24, and who then adds a delete against the explicit rule in LocalFiles.kt:276-279. At most this is a wording polish (for example "by copy, then clearing the source"), not a defect.

claim: EntryId.of was added but the identical inline ContentType-to-EntryId mapping it replaces stays in LibraryEngine
reason: The claimed duplicate is only partly real, and the failure it predicts is hypothetical. MergedDuplicateCarryMigration.entryIds (MergedDuplicateCarryMigration.kt:94-97) is a different rule: an exhaustive `when` that maps ALL to null and returns a pair. Because it is exhaustive, adding a new ContentType value breaks the build there, so it cannot silently drift. The LibraryEngine.kt:853-856 `when` predates the range (54d798ecd is an ancestor of 95f5c787a). The ledger already has a 'holds' row refuting this exact site: rows reach manualPositionsByCategory only through Long.toContentType() in ContentTypeColumn.kt, which yields only MANGA or NOVELS and throws on anything else, so the two opposite fallbacks never see an input where they disagree. The new failure scenario (a future anime type) would need a new EntryId subtype, a change to the DB column mapping (which throws on unknown values), and a change to EntryId.of itself. EntryId.of (EntryId.kt:28) is a non-exhaustive `if` that would also silently send the new type to Manga, so calling it from LibraryEngine would not protect against the scenario either. What is left is a cosmetic chance to call EntryId.of at one inline site, with no behaviour difference today.

claim: Each type's listing and the sync's held() separately restate the 'missing group members' gate before calling LocalGroups.missingMembers
reason: The rule that decides which folders are skipped exists once, in LocalGroups.missingMembers (domain/.../LocalGroups.kt:53-54). It returns foldersOf(series) filtered to `it != series && it !in rootNames`. The gate at each site (`foldersOf(series).none { it != series }` at LocalChapterTombstonesImpl.kt:37, `folders.any { it != manga.url }` at LocalSource.kt:324, `folders.any { it != novelPath }` at LocalNovelSource.kt:129) is true exactly when that filter is already empty. So with the gate or without it, missingMembers gives the same answer. The gate only skips a root listing that cannot change the result, and it carries no rule of its own. That is a performance shortcut, not a restated rule. Removing any copy, or loosening it as in the finder's example, gives the same skipped set as before. A listing and held() can only disagree if someone writes a new, stricter rule into a gate, which is a hypothetical future edit, not a defect in the current code. Failure handling is also consistent. All three listings throw rather than return an empty set when the root is unreadable: listedOrFail throws (LocalSource.kt:523-525), the novel source throws when the root is null and lists through reikai.storage.list, and rootNames throws FolderUnreadableException (LocalChapterFiles.kt:36-38). LocalSeriesRelink.kt:98 calls missingMembers with no gate at all and is equivalent for the same reason. Per code-quality.md, three one-line equivalent shortcuts over a shared kernel do not justify a helper.

claim: Two repositories now read and write the local_volume_pick table, and loadedPicks restates VolumePickRepositoryImpl's per-type read
reason: The duplication exists: LocalVolumeRepositoryImpl.kt:98-100 re-reads local_volume_pickQueries.getAll and filters by type, which VolumePickRepositoryImpl.kt:32-40 already does as a held StateFlow, and restorePick writes the table through the new setIfAbsent (local_volume_pick.sq:18-20). But the stated failure cannot happen silently. Both repositories call the same SQLDelight-generated queries, so re-keying picks by address or adding a column changes the generated getAll mapper and the setIfAbsent/set parameters, and both files stop compiling. The type encoding is the shared toDbValue in both. The separate read has a reason: backup (LocalVolumeBackup.kt:25) and relink (LocalSeriesRelink.kt:166) need a fresh one-shot read, and VolumePickRepository only offers an Eagerly-started StateFlow that begins as emptyMap. restorePick also needs local_move's address-to-id lookup, which already lives beside it. The interface KDoc (LocalVolumes.kt:51) names VolumePickRepository as the owner. What remains is a minor placement point (these two methods could sit on VolumePickRepository), not a defect with a realistic failure.

claim: The kept-state backup pass is written once per creator, while its sibling local-volume pass got a shared helper
reason: The two copies are each a three-line call into a kernel the two creators already share, `writeRows`. What differs between them is the type-specific receiver: BackupManga.chapterTombstones and BackupNovel.chapterTombstones. MangaBackupCreator.kt:131-136 and NovelBackupCreator.kt:125-130 match the claim. The rule is pinned at the conformance-test rung that content-layer.md allows. The proposed failure, reading tombstones before chapters, is exactly what ChapterTombstoneBackupTest.kt:80-95 catches. That test is `a chapter captured between the backup's two reads is still in the backup`, run with @EnumSource over both creators. Its decorator inserts the tombstone and deletes the chapter inside getByOwners. If someone reordered the reads in either creator, the tombstone read would come back empty and the chapter read would miss /c5, so that type's case would go red. The finder concedes the two copies cannot drift silently, so this is a style preference about a one-liner, not a defect.

claim: Loose-files mode sits outside the local-volume backup kernel on both the write and restore side, restating its isLocal gate
reason: The KDoc at LocalVolumeBackup.kt:9-13 lists exactly what the kernel writes: saved order and names, volumes from other folders, and the chip. It does not mention loose files, so it does not claim more than it covers. Loose files are manga-only, and that is recorded. The LooseFiles KDoc says so (LocalVolumes.kt:11-14), and the Decisions in docs/dev/subsystems/local-novels.md:71 say 'Loose files is not offered for novels'. Putting it in the two-type kernel would need a capability slot or a nullable field, which content-layer.md forbids. The trailing manga-only line next to the kernel (MangaBackupCreator.kt:139-140, MangaRestorer.kt:112) is the shape those rules point to. The failure scenario is hypothetical: someone changes the kernel's key or gate and misses the adjacent line in the same function. LocalFilesBackupRoundTripTest.kt:104-110 also pins the loose-files round trip.

claim: BackupTombstoneSession restates BackupReadingSession without its url
reason: Both shapes exist as stated (BackupChapterTombstone.kt:47-50, BackupReadingSession.kt:10-15, ChapterTombstones.kt:16). Nothing is wrong with them today. The reading log row is chapter_id, ended_at, duration (reading_session.sq:5,15), and the tombstone carries exactly ended_at and duration. The finder's failure case (a field added to the session later) is hypothetical. Sharing the Kotlin shape would not prevent it either. Tombstone sessions live in their own tables (chapter_tombstone.sq:25,53), and plain SQL moves them: captureMangaSessions/captureNovelSessions copy SELECT FROM reading_session (sq:86-89,116-119), and applyMangaSessions/applyNovelSessions INSERT INTO reading_session (sq:237-240,274-277). A new column would need edits to those tables and statements whatever the Kotlin class looked like. That SQL also explains the millis Long rather than Instant: ChapterTombstoneRepositoryImpl.kt:38-40 builds TombstoneSession straight from the query columns. Reusing BackupReadingSession would only repeat, in every session, a url (its required field 1) that the parent BackupChapterTombstone.url (field 1) already gives. The KDoc at ChapterTombstones.kt:15 already names the coupling ('as the reading log keeps it'). At most this is a missing-comment nit, not a defect.

claim: The 'hold a local series' lock across its parse and row sync' rule is written once per engine and pinned by two unrelated tests, not one conformance test
reason: The audit ledger already holds this finding as refuted ('holds' row on UpdateMangaFromRemote.kt:122). The rule lives in one place: both engines call the same kernel, LocalSeriesLocks.withSeries, which owns the key, the case folding, the blocked-series refusal and the wait. That is the first rung of the pin-once ladder. Only the dispatch differs per engine. Manga uses an isLocal() branch in the RK island (UpdateMangaFromRemote.kt:119-133), because a typed capability cannot reach source-api's Source. Novels use the LockedSeriesSource capability (NovelRefresh.kt:124-125, LocalNovelSource.kt:117-118). No 'twin of' marker exists, so no pin is owed. The claim that the novel side's real lock is unpinned is wrong. LocalNovelFolderTest.kt:63-84 builds a real LocalNovelSource over a real LocalSeriesLocks and shows that source.locked("Saga") makes a withSeries(NOVELS, "saga") holder wait. That test covers the real lock and its key folding. NovelRefreshTest.kt:152-160 pins that the refresh does its parse and its row sync inside that hold. LocalMovesUnderLockTest.kt:72-78 names both novel pins in its KDoc. The Result.failure versus throw difference is only Mihon's Result shape: per the ledger, the novel throw reaches NovelUpdateWorker's shared checkUpdateEntry handling. local-novels.md:19 documents the one-lock rule for both types.

claim: 'Open the series' details screen on Organize files' preview' is written out at two call sites instead of as one EntryVolumes verb
reason: The two sites do repeat the same three lines (LibraryTab.kt:845-847, EntryDetailsContent.kt:316-318), but the claim that the order makes this a rule does not hold. requestOrganize (EntryVolumes.kt:239-241) writes into an app-wide MutableStateFlow map, and organizeRequests (EntryVolumes.kt:244-245) hands each entry over once, whenever the details screen starts collecting (EntryDetailsContent.kt:234). A request made after the push would still be picked up, because a StateFlow replays its current value and the screen only composes on a later frame. Both steps are already shared EntryVolumes verbs, so the repeated part is two lines of glue. The project's code-quality rule says three similar lines beat a helper. Neither site is a manga/novel twin: both take the content type as a value. The gates differ because the operations differ (a combine returns a move result, a split returns the id of the series it created), so the difference is not drift. A third caller, EntryDetailsDialog.kt:111, uses requestOrganize without a push, which shows the two verbs are meant to be used separately.

claim: EntryId.of was added as the kernel for 'entry of this type and row id', but a hand-written copy in LibraryEngine treats ALL the opposite way
reason: The failure described cannot happen. manualPositionsByCategory (LibraryEngine.kt:850-857) only sees rows from manualOrderRepository.subscribeAll() (LibraryEngine.kt:190-193). Those rows go through LibraryManualOrderRepositoryImpl.mapPosition (line 69-70), which calls Long.toContentType() (data/.../ContentTypeColumn.kt:16-20). That function maps only 0 to MANGA and 1 to NOVELS and throws on any other value. The write side, toDbValue (ContentTypeColumn.kt:10-14), throws on ContentType.ALL, so an ALL row can never be stored. Every in-tree ManualOrderPosition constructor passes MANGA or NOVELS (NovelRestorer.kt:266, RestoreRepositoryImpl.kt:89) or copies a type out of an existing tile (LibraryManualOrder.kt:76). So on the only path that exists, the two fallbacks never disagree. What is left is a small DRY nit: one hand-written two-branch when that could call EntryId.of. That is not a defect, and the code predates the range.
